title: Problem 1.3 (Bárány–Kalai, Problem 6.6 in [6])
statement_text: Determine or estimate the least integer $f=f(d,s,t)$ such that for any set $P$ of $f$ points in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ there is a partition $P=A\cup B$ such that any $s$-convex set containing $A$ must intersect any $t$-convex set containing $B$.
context_text: This is a generalization of Radon's theorem to unions of convex sets, posed by Kalai in the 1970s and reiterated by Bárány and Kalai in their 2022 survey [6]. Bárány and Kalai showed $f(d,s,t)$ is finite via a Ramsey-type argument but noted the upper bound obtained is horrible; the correct behavior of this function remained unknown for more than fifty years despite substantial attention.
paper_contribution: Proves the near-optimal upper bound $f(d,s,t)=O(dst\log(st+1))$, settling the open problem.
notes: Originally posed by Kalai in the 1970s; formally stated as Problem 6.6 in the Bárány–Kalai 2022 Bulletin AMS survey. The abstract explicitly states the paper settles this open problem.
paper_title: Extended VC-dimension, and Radon and Tverberg type theorems for unions of convex sets

title: Problem 1.4
statement_text: Determine or estimate the least integer $f=f_{r}(d,s_{1},\ldots,s_{r})$ such that for any set $P$ of $f$ points in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ there is a partition into $r$ pairwise disjoint sets $P=\bigcup_{i=1}^{r}P_{i}$ such that for any family of sets $C_{1},\ldots,C_{r}$ with $P_{i}\subset C_{i}$ where $C_{i}$ is an $s_{i}$-convex set for every $i\in[r]$ we have that $\bigcap_{i=1}^{r}C_{i}\neq\emptyset$.
context_text: For an integer $s\geq 1$, a set $C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$ is $s$-convex if it is the union of $s$ convex sets. The two-part case is a problem of Kalai from the 1970s (problem 6.6 in the survey of Bárány and Kalai): determine the least $f(d,s,t)$ such that any $f$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ can be partitioned as $A\cup B$ so that any $s$-convex set containing $A$ intersects any $t$-convex set containing $B$; Bárány and Kalai showed finiteness via hypergraph Ramsey theory with a horrible bound. The present problem is its Tverberg-type generalization to $r$ parts. Radon's theorem is equivalent to $f(d,1,1)=d+2$ and Tverberg's theorem to $f_{r}(d,1,\ldots,1)=(r-1)(d+1)+1$. Using an extended (multi-part) VC-dimension argument, the paper proves $f(d,s,t)=O(dst\log(st+1))$ and $f_{r}(d,s_{1},\ldots,s_{r})=O\left(dr^{2}\log r\cdot\prod_{i=1}^{r}s_{i}\cdot\ln(1+\prod_{i=1}^{r}s_{i})\right)$, and the proofs work in abstract separable convexity spaces with bounded Radon number. Following the paper, Chen et al. obtained the nearly matching lower bound $f_r(d,s,\ldots,s)\geq(d-2r+4)s^r$ for $d\geq 2r-2$; the exact determination remains open.
notes: The paper proves the upper bound $f_{r}(d,s_{1},\ldots,s_{r})=O\left(dr^{2}\cdot\log r\cdot\prod_{i=1}^{r}s_{i}\cdot\ln(1+\prod_{i=1}^{r}s_{i})\right)$ via Theorem 1.6, partially addressing this problem. A 2025 paper by Chen et al. (reference [9]) is titled 'A Tverberg-type problem of Kalai: Two negative answers to questions of Alon and Smorodinsky', suggesting specific sub-questions of this problem are attributed to the paper authors.
paper_title: Extended VC-dimension, and Radon and Tverberg type theorems for unions of convex sets
